applies_why: The judge is resolving a link by treating Matthew 1:16's isolated grammar as admitting two readings and labeling it underdetermined.
quote: UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: 'never verse by verse': either the judge must decide by the competing chains' footing rather than by one verse's ambiguity, or it may call the verse underdetermined on its own words while merely noting that the parties answered.
why: The judge labels Matthew 1:16 underdetermined because its isolated grammar admits both readings, which is a verse-by-verse ambiguity test instead of the required chain-against-chain weighing by footing.
